jobs.prompt: Build tools/split-module.mjs, the deterministic codemod that splits tools/swarm.mjs into modules as a PURE MOVE (no behavior change), using the scanner in tools/split-scan.mjs (read-only, in context: scanModule(text) -> { items, imports, exports, order }; each item has kind, names, exported, start, end, text, uses; dependencyGraph(items); topLevelNameIndex(items)). CLI: node tools/split-module.mjs plan FILE [--json]; node tools/split-module.mjs move FILE --to MODULE_PATH --names a,b,c [--dry-run] [--allow-back-references]; node tools/split-module.mjs verify FILE --to MODULE_PATH --original ORIGINAL_FILE. Also export the same operations as functions (planSplit, moveItems, verifyMove) for tests. plan: print the dependency layers of the top-level items, leaves first: layer 0 = items that use no other top-level item of the file (besides imports), layer 1 = items whose uses are all in earlier layers, and so on; items in a cycle form one strongly connected group listed together. Mark items that CANNOT move alone: a let or var that is reassigned anywhere in the file (an assignment, increment or destructuring assignment to its name), an item that uses import.meta, __filename, __dirname or process.argv[1] directly, and the main entry statements at the bottom (expression statements). Output the layers with item names, line spans and sizes, and a suggested grouping into modules by name prefix and adjacency. move: take the named top-level items (and refuse unless every other top-level item they use is either an import of the file, a builtin global, another item in the same move, or already imported from a previously split module: unless --allow-back-references, a use of a name still defined in FILE is an error that lists the names). Create MODULE_PATH with: the SPDX header line if FILE has one, the import statements the moved items need (copy only the import specifiers actually used, keeping the original import lines for each source module and fixing relative paths when the new module lives in a different directory), the moved items' text EXACTLY as in the original (byte for byte, in their original order), and export statements so every moved name is exported. Rewrite FILE: remove the moved items (and their attached comments) leaving no extra blank lines beyond what the original had between items, add one import line for the moved names from the new module right after the last existing import, and for every moved name that FILE exported before keep exporting it with a re-export line (export { name } from the new module path) so that every other file importing from FILE keeps working. A moved name used by FILE items stays visible through the import. Keep the file deterministic (names sorted where the tool must choose an order). verify: prove the move is lossless: the new module's item texts concatenated equal the original items' texts byte for byte; the remaining FILE plus the moved items, with imports and re-exports ignored, equals the original FILE; node --check passes on both files (spawn node --check); every export name of the original FILE is still exported by FILE (directly or by re-export); and that the new module does not import FILE (no cycle). Return a result object and a non-zero exit code with a precise message on any mismatch. The move command runs verify itself before writing and writes nothing when it fails. Tests in tests/split-module.test.mjs with fixture mini programs in a temp dir: a leaf move, a move with an import used by the moved item, a move refused for a back reference, a move refused for a reassigned let, an item with import.meta refused, re-export keeps an importing file working (spawn node to import it), dry-run writes nothing, verify catches a hand-altered copy, plan layers a small cycle as one group; and a test on the real tools/swarm.mjs: plan finishes in under 5 seconds and prints at least one layer-0 item, and a dry-run move of one layer-0 function to a temp module path reports ok without touching tools/swarm.mjs. No dependencies: node:fs, node:path, node:child_process, node:test, node:assert only. Do not edit tools/swarm.mjs. No token-shaped literals. ignoreTests reason: only new files are written.
